selected_topology: protected canonical knowledge -> one-shot private projection -> offline release court -> local sanitized registry -> read-only prior art
claim_boundary: This is an architecture-suitability judgment, not an empirical superiority claim and not evidence that the planned product exists.
independence_boundary: The participants were separate agent turns with distinct assigned identities. This establishes procedural separation only, not authenticated independent-human, organizational, legal, privacy, or licensing approval.

participants.function: preserve the user source, schedule the court, and author the implementation DAG
inspect current-main code, tests, history, and implementation status without edits
make the strongest evidence-bounded case for the proposed product
search for contradictions, authority gaps, leakage, poisoning, lock-in, and failure modes without edits
assess architecture fit, current reusable primitives, and the divergent Phase 3 prototype without edits
adjudicate candidate topologies, claims, adverse evidence, amendments, dissent, and appeal conditions without edits
independently lint the authored DAG and cross-check scopes, tests, dependencies, seals, and claims without authoring the plan

scout.position: Current main has valuable append-only events, bounded memory, court, learning, and challenger machinery, but no implemented Obsidian projector, stable Idea/IdeaPass model, private/shared knowledge registry, or safe-release gateway.
scout.verified_test_receipt: 92 focused memory, learning, court, challenger, and projection tests passed in the Scout's read-only workspace.
scout.adverse_finding: Committed .autopilot/lessons are an existing cross-repository portability path for node, head, actor, and detail fields without the proposed release court.

advocate.position: Adapt current primitives into a staged local product: canonical private knowledge, immutable repeated passes, complete typed lifecycle edges, rebuildable private views, offline release bundles, and a local sanitized registry.
advocate.strongest_value_case: The design can reduce forgotten alternatives and repeated ideation while preserving why work returned to an earlier stage; that outcome remains a hypothesis until controlled evaluation.

cross_examiner.position: The credible first release stops at a private projector unless authority, disclosure, retention, and independent release evidence close the demonstrated gaps.
adverse_findings: ConstraintEnvelope narrowing omits sensitive scope and budget dimensions.
Authority registration and use are not sufficiently content-bound, collision-safe, or registry-backed at the actual effect boundary.
Lesson intake can admit weak provenance and active free text into challenger construction.
Secret scanning is not an IP, privacy, or nondisclosure proof.
Current JSON/HTML projection is direct-writing and can expose objectives or hypotheses without the planned classification boundary.
Existing appeal and replan limits do not implement unlimited stable idea passes.

expert.position: Use current-main contracts as the authority and treat the Phase 3 branch as a pattern donor only.
expert.prototype_assessment: The divergent prototype contains useful transactional projection, conflict, public/private, and federation mechanics, but it lacks the required stable IdeaPass lifecycle and its Canvas evidence omits relationship edges. It is not merge-ready.
expert.safety_warning: No generic scanner can prove that an abstraction discloses no proprietary or private information; structural minimization, provenance/taint, adversarial tests, and an independent release decision are all required.

candidate_topologies.topology: repository Markdown or Obsidian vault is canonical authority
candidate_topologies.reason: Mutable files, titles, paths, links, and plugins cannot supply the append-only typed authority, deterministic replay, or point-in-time evidence contract.

candidate_topologies.topology: direct projector over the current mixed stores
candidate_topologies.reason: Mission, court, memory, prompt, scheduler, and lesson records do not yet share one reducible authority; a direct merge would conceal contradictions and sensitivity boundaries.

candidate_topologies.topology: protected canonical knowledge plus one-shot private projector
candidate_topologies.reason: It provides the requested history and graph with the smallest authority and disclosure surface and works without Obsidian.

candidate_topologies.topology: private canonical knowledge, offline release court, local sanitized registry, and inert read-only prior art
candidate_topologies.reason: It tests cross-repository learning while keeping publication, activation, and private source material outside the authorized path.

candidate_topologies.topology: automatic remote or public shared registry
candidate_topologies.reason: Authenticated external identity, durable retention/takedown, transport threats, revocation, and exact-candidate nondisclosure evidence are unresolved.

candidate_topologies.topology: wholesale merge of the Phase 3 prototype
candidate_topologies.reason: The branch is divergent prior art and does not satisfy current-main authority, lifecycle, or evidence contracts.

candidate_topologies.topology: required external SaaS, Obsidian plugin, Sync, embedding, or watcher
candidate_topologies.reason: These dependencies are unnecessary for the local product and lack admitted product, security, license, retention, and lock-in evidence.

atomic_claims.claim: The tool must operate across repositories without raw remote URLs, local paths, or repository names becoming portable identity.
atomic_claims.verification: rename, clone-path, Unicode, Windows, tenant-canary, and subject-commit tests
atomic_claims.rollback: disable the federation and identity adapter while preserving opaque record history

atomic_claims.claim: Current append-only event and memory primitives may be adapted into one protected canonical knowledge authority.
atomic_claims.verification: authority inventory, chain corruption, concurrency, replay, backup, restore, and dual-owner rejection
atomic_claims.rollback: disable the new store adapter and retain events plus migration receipts

atomic_claims.claim: A private Obsidian-compatible graph should cover all permitted material lifecycle records and relationships.
atomic_claims.verification: official-source admission, required-record coverage, byte-identical rebuild, typed-link, and Obsidian-absent tests
atomic_claims.rollback: delete and rebuild the derived vault with the previous renderer

atomic_claims.claim: Obsidian, Markdown, Bases, Canvas, dashboards, and generated indices must remain disposable non-authoritative views.
atomic_claims.verification: source-head binding, stale-cursor, human-edit conflict, staging, crash, and rebuild tests
atomic_claims.rollback: discard staging/output and regenerate from verified canonical state

atomic_claims.claim: One stable Idea must have immutable, ordered IdeaPass records.
atomic_claims.verification: three-pass identity, immutability, ordinal, collision, and replay fixtures
atomic_claims.rollback: disable the runtime version without rewriting prior passes

atomic_claims.claim: An idea may re-enter the workflow any number of times.
atomic_claims.qualification: There is no fixed semantic pass limit, but every new pass remains subject to authority, evidence, resource leases, duplicate-failure detection, and stopping conditions.
atomic_claims.verification: multiple remand, appeal, incident, regression, deferred-trigger, and later-evidence paths
atomic_claims.rollback: stop creating successor passes while preserving every prior return fact

atomic_claims.claim: Every semantic return to an earlier stage must retain its source gate, requested destination, reason, evidence, actor, prior pass, and successor.
atomic_claims.verification: point-in-time path reconstruction with zero missing mandatory backward reasons
atomic_claims.rollback: quarantine incomplete traces; never infer or fabricate a reason

atomic_claims.claim: Idea, work, candidate, verified deliverable, delivery, outcome, signal, lesson, challenger, evaluation, and promotion are distinct append-only record types.
atomic_claims.verification: schema and mandatory-edge coverage with explicit not-applicable dispositions
atomic_claims.rollback: disable a faulty adapter while retaining the source record and adverse evidence

atomic_claims.claim: All eight specialist roles and all temporary court seats must be attributable in the graph.
atomic_claims.qualification: A record must label whether evidence is merely declared, a fixture, a model turn, a real read/effect, independently reproduced, or externally authenticated.
atomic_claims.rollback: downgrade the maturity label; never delete an episode to improve coverage

atomic_claims.claim: Champion, challenger, losing evaluation, counterexample, rejection, promotion, and rollback evidence should be linked so proposals are not needlessly repeated.
atomic_claims.verification: inert intake, provenance, conflict, held-out evaluation, rollback, and negative-result retrieval tests
atomic_claims.rollback: remove prior-art lookup from decision context while retaining citations and evaluation history

atomic_claims.claim: Cross-repository learning may enter a local shared registry only after a separate offline release decision.
atomic_claims.verification: synthetic license-clean bundle, independent disposition, revocation, tombstone, and cross-tenant tests
atomic_claims.rollback: revoke or tombstone the bundle and disable the registry adapter

atomic_claims.claim: Shared records must be newly composed structural allowlists rather than redacted copies of private records.
atomic_claims.verification: unknown-field rejection, provenance allowlist, body/link absence, determinism, and non-reversibility tests
atomic_claims.rollback: quarantine the candidate before registry admission

atomic_claims.claim: Secrets, private/customer data, proprietary expression, incompatible-license material, identity linkage, topology leakage, and prompt injection must fail closed at the release boundary.
atomic_claims.verification: direct, encoded, split-field, filename, count/timing, graph-neighbor, pseudonym-linkage, and poisoning fixtures with zero known bypass
atomic_claims.rollback: deny all release, preserve the private decision, and open a takedown case for any exposure

atomic_claims.claim: A release Curator and Judge must be distinct from the candidate author, affected champion, and each other.
atomic_claims.qualification: Agent identities establish procedural separation only; authenticated legal, privacy, licensing, or external-human authority remains a separate obligation.
atomic_claims.rollback: invalidate the disposition and return the candidate to private quarantine

atomic_claims.claim: Approved shared learning may be consulted only as inert, read-only prior art by Explorer and Optimizer.
atomic_claims.qualification: Reduced repeated ideation is an evaluation hypothesis, not an assumed outcome.
atomic_claims.verification: citation, local applicability, false-merge, duplicate-escape, no-execution, no-authority, and no-prompt-concatenation tests
atomic_claims.rollback: disable lookup while retaining the local evaluation record

atomic_claims.claim: Projection and registry updates must be deterministic, staged, cursor-bound, conflict-aware, reversible, and interruption-safe.
atomic_claims.verification: partial-write, stale-head, drift, conflict, tombstone, backup/restore, downgrade, and byte-identical rebuild tests
atomic_claims.rollback: disable the new renderer or registry version and rebuild from retained authority

atomic_claims.claim: Local portfolio use requires tenant, project-lineage, repository, pseudonym, and self-host recursion isolation.
atomic_claims.verification: tenant canaries, inference/count/linkage tests, source-tree validation, hop/depth/origin guards, and generated-output re-ingestion tests

atomic_claims.claim: The local product must work without Obsidian, an Obsidian account, Sync, a plugin, a watcher, or a network service.
atomic_claims.verification: offline generic Markdown/YAML/JSON operation and missing-Obsidian tests
atomic_claims.rollback: retain the canonical and CLI surfaces while disabling optional view adapters

adverse_findings_adopted.finding: Current main does not implement the requested Obsidian/IdeaPass/shared-registry product.
evidence: repository-wide tracked source and test search at the sealed baseline

adverse_findings_adopted.finding: Authority narrowing and the actual effect boundary require repair before any projector or release authority is safe.
Existing Autopilot lessons are a committed portability path for repository/run details and must be quarantined without rewriting history.
Append-only provenance must not force retention of credentials, customer data, or legally erasable bodies.
Current Obsidian compatibility claims lack newly retained pinned official-source evidence in this tournament.

blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.amendment: Seal the full tournament and plan bundle.
blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.resolution: The manifest and verifier enumerate and verify the tournament README, objective, source register, results, architecture decision, implementation program, DAG, and executable-DAG README.

blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.amendment: Extend authority work through the actual effect boundary and outbox.
blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.resolution: AUTHORITY-020 owns the relevant authority, contract, effect, outbox, test, and evidence paths and requires registry-backed use-time validation.

blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.amendment: Close the existing Autopilot lesson-export path.
blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.resolution: LEARNING-030 inventories and quarantines existing details without rewriting history, blocks new unapproved instance export, and requires separate exposure/takedown receipts.

blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.amendment: Admit current official Obsidian product evidence before compatibility claims.
blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.resolution: OBSIDIAN-SOURCE-160 is an explicit predecessor of OBSIDIAN-VIEWS-300; unavailable evidence narrows the product to generic Markdown/YAML/JSON.

blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.amendment: Resolve retention, deletion, and takedown before canonical storage.
blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.resolution: RETENTION-170 separates immutable metadata and receipts from protected or erasable bodies and blocks STORE-200 until the policy and expert obligations are resolved.

blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.amendment: Use only synthetic, license-clean records before the exact release court.
blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.resolution: Release-candidate, gateway, registry, and qualification contracts forbid real private records before RELEASE-COURT-510.

blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.amendment: Keep independence and remote-publication claims honest.
blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.resolution: RELEASE-COURT-510 requires distinct procedural identities and retains docs/plan/BLOCKERS.md obligations; remote publication remains quarantined.

blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.amendment: Do not mark planning complete until judgment, documents, amendments, and seals exist.
blocking_amendments_and_resolutions.resolution: Planning becomes complete only when the final manifest verification passes; all implementation nodes remain not_started.

preserved_dissent: The Cross-Examiner's preferred MVP stops after private projection; even the local shared registry stays disabled until every authority, disclosure, retention, and release-court contract passes.
The Advocate considers a local sanitized registry necessary to test whether cross-repository prior art is useful.
The Expert warns that scanners cannot prove nondisclosure and that the Phase 3 branch is only a pattern donor.
The Scout identifies committed Autopilot lessons as an existing unsanitized portability risk requiring immediate predecessor work.

appeal_conditions.subject: automatic_remote_publication
appeal_conditions.condition: Materially new evidence closes authenticated identity, external retention/takedown, transport threats, disclosure qualification, revocation, and exact-candidate authority.
